title: The Message That Outlived Its Maker
scaffold_note: Decision scaffold assembled 2026-10-26 (JOB MIGRATION-3) from eo-ep3's own records only. A field the records do not settle ships OPEN with an empty rationale — intent is never invented. Coverage wording: every count in this package is a count of recorded decisions with reasons, not an observation of the rendered result.

objective.value: Chapter three of how information evolved on Earth: show the third archive — a mark on a wall, the first message stored outside every living body, still speaking to strangers forty thousand years after its maker died.
objective.rationale: The series spine applied to threshold 3 (STRUCT-2 H5, decided); the script doc's occasion frames the same claim — the hand stencil as the first message that needed no living carrier.
objective.source: archer reasoning (script docs v2/v3 + STRUCT-2 audit, 2026-10-24)

message.value: "About 40,000 years ago, people began leaving marks on cave walls — and for the first time, information could live outside every living body and speak to strangers long after its maker was gone." (Essence, ≤8 words: 'A mark can outlive its maker.')
message.rationale: The one learning sentence (T-17); the v2 cold restatement matched it and passed. The doc itself logs the distinction between the sentence's 'for the first time' (the category shift) and the spoken lines' 'one of the first' (the claim fix) — a decision, not a slip.
message.record: files/short-eo03-first-message-script-v2.md — 'The one thing the viewer learns (T-17)' + 'T-17 audit + cold restatement' (PASS); carried unchanged into the v3 build script

story_structure.value: Problem–Agitation–Solution (a deliberate variation from Ep.1/Ep.2's And–But–Therefore). PROBLEM: every message so far needs a living carrier (L3). AGITATION: carriers die; when the last rememberer dies, the message dies (L4). SOLUTION: put the message on the wall, where it waits for strangers (L5–L7) — at a price named in L8–L9 (it cannot travel). Villain (N-06), named: the dying witness. Intended feeling: unease in the dark of the cave, then awe.
story_structure.rationale: Declared in the v2 script doc's narrative declaration (N-04/N-06/N-03, carried from v1, re-checked against v2 lines) and built unchanged in v3/v4.

hook_form.value: Prediction hook (N-01): L1 shows an act finishing — a hand pressed flat, red dust blown over it, the time anchor ('forty thousand years ago') at the END of the line — whose completion is not predictable: the setup reads as art; the payoff is storage, a message that needs no living carrier (L5, L7). Payoff lines named: L2 (the reveal), L7 (the statement). Cold test: PASS.
hook_form.rationale: Logged in the v2 Phase 1 Narrative Gate (N-01 first-line cold test, PASS); the v2 opener was rewritten action-first with the reason recorded in both Ep.3's and Ep.4's scripts (differentiate from Ep.4's temporal opener) — STRUCT-2 H1 scores it EXEMPLARY.

delivery_structure.value: Scene-led narration with measured inter-line breaths and a three-archive bookend: present-tense act (L1, window 1.95–7.64 s; words from 1.42 s) → proof beat, the real Pettakere photograph full-bleed (L2, 8.04–12.05 s) → problem (L3, 12.45–18.11 s) → agitation (L4, 18.56–23.19 s, mid-line plate cut carriers→dead fire at 'the message dies too') → solution statement (L5, 23.69–27.54 s) → reception/proof, the longest line (L6, 27.94–35.93 s, 22 words) → naming (L7, 36.38–38.92 s) → price pair (L8 pull-back, 39.52–42.42 s; L9, 42.82–46.08 s) → three-archive bookend recap with a scene state per phrase (L10, 46.53–52.88 s: savanna → carriers → wall) → spoken bridge (L11, 53.38–57.74 s) → end card to 62.34 s. Line windows are separated by measured gaps of 0.40–0.60 s (PLAN timeline); words: phrases of ≤3 words, cumulative arrival at the spoken moment, clearing before the next phrase, key words amber at +18% with overshoot pop, 25 words with decided choreography. The bed is a low synth-pad cave bed ducked ≈13 dB throughout.
delivery_structure.rationale: The delivery pattern is the one the v4 artifact demonstrably performs: the PLAN timeline's line windows and gaps, the per-phrase scene states, the mid-line plate cut and the word system are all in-package records (PLAN + DR-E3G records), and the beat order is the story_structure's Problem–Agitation–Solution rendered as delivery. Decided as the delivery structure of record: the pattern below is measured off the delivered artifact itself (locked line windows, phrase system and gap schedule all in this package's own records) — it ratifies the delivery the piece actually has. No separate researched pause-map / Stage-2 delivery pass was ever performed for this piece; a future delivery retrofit amends this field by a new dated decision, it does not silently overwrite it.

scene_decomposition.value: The scene stays ONE self-contained file (scene/index.html, 7,195,184 B, sha256 9da54631…), and its decomposition is the compartment inventory the file itself embodies — (1) plate layer: generated plates created from PLATE_URIS (blow, wall, carriers, embers, visitors, dawnland, savanna) plus the real Pettakere photograph component (photoEl/photoCap, full-bleed at L2's 'still there today') and the speaking-glow component (glowEl, L6); (2) word layer: span.word elements generated per PLAN phrase (160 words, ≤3-word phrases, per-word cx/cy/size/colour/shadow) with label elements ('40,000 YEARS AGO' L1, 'IT WAITS IN THE DARK' L5); (3) container compartment: opening card (blow plate + EARTH ONE + title, 1.6 s) and end card (wall plate + FOLLOW + NEXT tease 'A SONG REMEMBERS WHAT WORDS FORGET', 3.4 s) and the EARTH ONE bug (per-scene ink); (4) scene engine: PLAN (timeline, phrases, words) + CONFIG (sceneForLine per line, L4 plateCut carriers→embers, cards, labels, bug colours) + the plateAt/lineAt renderer; (5) audio compartment: #mix (embedded guide-era programme audio; the CLONE-VERIFIED candidate lives in audio/); (6) in-page decision-record layer: #decisions JSON (24 records, coverage 24/24) with the 160 word decisions in its word_decisions array, plus the production-context panel (#ctxpanel); (7) player chrome: #chrome (playbtn, bar/fill, clock), #tooltip. No physical split into separate HTML/CSS/JS files is performed — the single-file form is the delivered form.
scene_decomposition.rationale: Every compartment is named from the shipped file's own PLAN/CONFIG data and its DEC records, counted in the package's element coverage (24/24, incl. 9 image plates, 3 element-layer components, 5 word placements, 3 container records); the decomposition records the engine's actual architecture, not a rebuild plan.
